questions.stem: A study investigates whether the number of hours spent studying helps explain students’ exam scores. The explanatory variable is:
options: the number of students
the exam date
hours spent studying
exam score
questions.explanation: The explanatory variable is the one used to explain or predict the other, here hours of study. The exam score is the response variable, the one that is thought to change in response.

questions.stem: On a scatterplot, the response variable is plotted on:
options: either axis, by choice
both axes
the vertical axis
the horizontal axis
questions.explanation: By convention the explanatory variable goes on the horizontal (x) axis and the response variable on the vertical (y) axis.

questions.stem: A scatterplot is the appropriate display for:
options: the distribution of one numerical variable
the frequencies of one categorical variable
comparing one variable across several groups
the association between two numerical variables
questions.explanation: Each point on a scatterplot shows one subject’s pair of values, so it displays how two numerical variables vary together. One numerical variable needs a histogram or boxplot instead.

questions.stem: Two numerical variables have a positive association. This means that:
options: as one increases, the other tends to increase
as one increases, the other tends to decrease
one variable causes the other to increase
every value of both variables is positive
questions.explanation: Positive association describes the direction of the trend: larger values of one variable go with larger values of the other. It says nothing about cause, or about the signs of the values.

questions.stem: When describing an association, its form tells us:
options: whether the points rise or fall from left to right
how closely the points cluster about the pattern
which variable causes the change in the other
whether the pattern is linear or non-linear
questions.explanation: Form is the shape of the pattern, such as linear or curved. Rising or falling is direction, and how closely the points cluster is strength.

questions.stem: The strength of an association describes:
options: how closely points follow the pattern
how steep the line of good fit is
whether the points rise or fall
how many points are on the scatterplot
questions.explanation: A strong association has points tightly clustered about the trend; a weak one has them widely scattered. Steepness is the slope, which is a different feature.

questions.stem: The statement “association does not imply causation” means that:
options: variables that are associated can never be related by cause and effect
causation can be shown by finding a strong association
a weak association always means one variable causes the other
an association alone does not show that one variable changes the other
questions.explanation: An association may be caused by other variables, or be coincidence, so it is not evidence of cause on its own. It does not rule out cause either: some associated variables are causally linked.

questions.stem: Using a line of good fit to predict a value within the range of the data is called:
options: extrapolation
causation
transformation
interpolation
questions.explanation: Interpolation predicts inside the range of the explanatory variable that was used to fit the line. Predicting outside that range is extrapolation, which is less reliable.

questions.stem: Extrapolation is:
options: predicting within the range of the data
removing outliers from a scatterplot
fitting a curve instead of a straight line
predicting outside the range of the data
questions.explanation: Extrapolation uses the line beyond the data, assuming the trend carries on there. That assumption may fail, which is why extrapolation is less reliable than interpolation.

questions.stem: A line of good fit drawn by eye should:
options: join the first and the last data points, whatever lies between
pass through as many data points as possible
always pass through the origin
follow the trend, with about as many points above as below
questions.explanation: A line of good fit shows the overall trend, so the points should be balanced on either side along its length. Joining the end points or hitting many points exactly can give a line that misses the trend.

questions.stem: If a scatterplot shows no association between two variables, the points:
options: lie on a horizontal straight line across the plot
lie on a vertical straight line
fall steadily from left to right
show no clear rising or falling pattern
questions.explanation: With no association, knowing one variable tells us nothing about the other, so the points form a shapeless cloud. Points falling steadily show a negative association.

questions.stem: A line of good fit has equation y = 150 − 4.2x. The association between x and y is:
options: positive
non-linear
none at all
negative
questions.explanation: The slope, −4.2, is negative, so y tends to decrease as x increases. The line is straight, which describes a linear form.

questions.stem: Ice-cream sales and the number of drownings at Victorian beaches are positively associated. The most likely explanation is that:
options: both increase in hot weather
eating ice cream causes drowning
drownings cause ice-cream sales to rise
ice-cream sales are higher on cool days
questions.explanation: Hot weather brings more people to beaches to swim and to buy ice cream, so a third variable drives both. This is why an association alone is not evidence of cause.

questions.stem: A line of good fit for exam score against hours of study is score = 42 + 5.5 × hours. The slope tells us that:
options: on average, each extra hour of study goes with 5.5 more marks
on average, each extra mark needs 5.5 more hours of study
a student who studies no hours is predicted to score 5.5
each hour of study causes exactly 5.5 more marks
questions.explanation: The slope is the predicted change in the response for a one-unit increase in the explanatory variable, so 5.5 marks per hour on average. It describes a trend in the data, not a guaranteed causal effect.

questions.stem: For the line of good fit score = 42 + 5.5 × hours, the intercept tells us that:
options: a student needs 42 hours of study to pass
a student who studies for 0 hours is predicted to score 42
each hour of study adds 42 marks on average
the highest score in the data is 42
questions.explanation: The intercept is the predicted response when the explanatory variable is 0. Adding marks for each hour is the role of the slope, 5.5.

questions.stem: Using the line of good fit score = 42 + 5.5 × hours, the predicted score for a student who studies for 6 hours is:
questions.explanation: Score = 42 + 5.5 × 6 = 42 + 33 = 75. The value 33 is only the contribution from study, without the intercept.

questions.stem: Researchers want to predict a person’s height from their arm span. The explanatory and response variables are:
options: height is explanatory and arm span is the response
both variables are explanatory
both variables are responses
arm span is explanatory and height is the response
questions.explanation: The variable we use to predict is explanatory, so arm span goes on the horizontal axis and height, the variable being predicted, is the response.

questions.stem: The points on a scatterplot rise from left to right and lie close to a straight line. The association is best described as:
options: strong, positive and non-linear
strong, positive and linear
weak, positive and linear
strong, negative and linear
questions.explanation: Rising left to right is positive, a straight-line pattern is linear, and points close to the line show a strong association.

questions.stem: The points on a scatterplot fall from left to right in a roughly straight band, but are widely scattered. The association is:
options: weak, positive and linear
weak, negative and non-linear
weak, negative and linear
strong, negative and linear
questions.explanation: Falling from left to right means a negative direction, a straight band is linear, and wide scatter makes it weak.

questions.stem: A line of good fit passes through (10, 60) and (30, 20). Its equation is:
questions.explanation: Slope = (20 − 60) ÷ (30 − 10) = −2. Then 60 = a − 2 × 10 gives a = 80. Using the point’s y-value, 60, as the intercept forgets that x = 10 there.

questions.stem: For children aged 2 to 10, a line of good fit is height (cm) = 80 + 6 × age (years). It predicts a height of 260 cm at age 30. Why is this prediction unreliable?
options: It extrapolates far beyond the ages in the data.
It interpolates within the ages in the data.
The slope of the line is positive.
The intercept of the line is not zero.
questions.explanation: Children stop growing in their teens, so the trend in ages 2 to 10 does not continue to age 30. Predicting so far outside the data is extrapolation.

questions.stem: A line of good fit was drawn for data with x-values from 5 to 25. Which prediction is an interpolation?
options: a prediction at x = 18
a prediction at x = 30
a prediction at x = 0
a prediction at x = 2
questions.explanation: Interpolation stays inside the data range, from 5 to 25, so only x = 18 qualifies. The others lie outside the range and are extrapolations.

questions.stem: A survey finds that students who eat breakfast tend to get higher marks. Which conclusion is valid?
options: Higher marks cause students to eat breakfast.
There is no relationship between the two variables.
The variables are associated, but other factors may explain it.
Eating breakfast causes students’ marks to rise.
questions.explanation: A survey can show association, but other factors, such as home routines, may affect both breakfast and marks. Showing cause needs a controlled experiment.

questions.stem: The points on a scatterplot rise steeply at first and then level off. The form of the association is:
options: linear
non-linear
positive and linear
negative
questions.explanation: A pattern that bends, rising steeply then flattening, is curved, so its form is non-linear. Negative describes direction, not form.

questions.stem: A line of good fit passes through (0, 12) and (8, 36). Its equation is:
questions.explanation: The point (0, 12) gives the intercept, 12. The slope is (36 − 12) ÷ 8 = 3. Dividing 36 by 8 gives 4.5, which ignores the intercept.

questions.stem: For a car trip, a line of good fit is fuel used (L) = 0.5 + 0.08 × distance (km). The slope tells us that:
options: the car always uses 0.08 L of fuel on every trip
about 0.08 L more fuel is used for each extra kilometre
about 0.08 km is travelled for each litre of fuel
about 0.5 L more fuel is used for each extra kilometre
questions.explanation: The slope is the change in the response, litres, per one-unit increase in the explanatory variable, kilometres. Reading it as kilometres per litre turns the rate upside down.

questions.stem: Using the line of good fit y = 12 + 3x, the value of x that gives a predicted y of 30 is:
questions.explanation: Solve 12 + 3x = 30: 3x = 18, so x = 6. Dividing 30 by 3 to get 10 ignores the intercept.

questions.stem: A line of good fit for used cars is value ($) = 32 000 − 2600 × age (years). The 32 000 is best interpreted as:
options: the highest value of any car in the data
the predicted value of a new car, at age 0
the yearly fall in value of a car
the age at which a car is worth nothing
questions.explanation: The intercept is the predicted response when the explanatory variable is 0, here a car of age 0. The yearly fall in value is the slope, $2600.

questions.stem: A line of good fit is height (cm) = 50 + 0.8 × time (days). The predicted growth over one week is:
options: 0.8 cm
7 cm
5.6 cm
questions.explanation: Growth over 7 days is the slope times the change in time: 0.8 × 7 = 5.6 cm. The value 55.6 cm is the predicted height after a week, not the growth.

questions.stem: Which pair of variables is most likely to show a negative association?
options: hours worked and pay earned at a fixed rate
daily temperature and ice-cream sales
the age of a car and its resale value
a person’s height and their arm span
questions.explanation: Older cars tend to be worth less, so as age goes up, value tends to go down. The other pairs tend to rise together, a positive association.

questions.stem: For days between 15 °C and 35 °C, a kiosk’s line of good fit is sales = −120 + 18 × temperature. Which statement is correct?
options: Predicting sales at 25 °C is extrapolation, giving 330.
Predicting sales at 25 °C is interpolation, giving 450.
Predicting sales at 25 °C is interpolation, giving 330.
Predicting sales at 40 °C is interpolation, giving 600.
questions.explanation: The value 25 °C lies inside the range 15 to 35 °C, so it is interpolation, and −120 + 18 × 25 = 330. The value 450 forgets the intercept, and 40 °C lies outside the data.

questions.stem: A kiosk’s line of good fit, from days between 15 °C and 35 °C, is sales = −120 + 18 × temperature. The intercept of −120 has no practical meaning because:
options: an intercept is only meaningful when it equals 0
0 °C is outside the data, and sales cannot be negative
the slope of 18 is too large for the data
the line has a positive slope, so it cannot cross the axis
questions.explanation: The intercept is the prediction at 0 °C, well outside the 15 to 35 °C data, and a negative number of sales is impossible. It fixes the position of the line but is not a sensible prediction.

questions.stem: Data set A has a line of good fit with slope 5 and data set B has one with slope 0.5. Which statement is correct?
options: Set A has the stronger association, as its slope is larger.
Set B has the stronger association, as its slope is smaller.
Both have equally strong associations, as both slopes are positive.
The slopes alone do not show which association is stronger.
questions.explanation: Strength is about how closely the points cluster about the line, not how steep the line is. A steep line can fit widely scattered points, and a gentle one can fit tightly clustered points.

questions.stem: For a sample of house fires, the number of fire trucks attending and the cost of the damage show a strong positive association. Which statement is correct?
options: Sending more fire trucks causes more damage to occur.
More damage causes more fire trucks to be sent later.
The two variables have no relationship with each other.
The size of the fire is likely to affect both variables.
questions.explanation: Bigger fires both bring more trucks and cause more damage, so a third variable explains the association. The data show association, not that trucks cause damage.

questions.stem: A line of good fit passes through (2, 7.5) and (10, 3.5). The predicted value of y when x = 6 is:
questions.explanation: Slope = (3.5 − 7.5) ÷ (10 − 2) = −0.5. Then 7.5 = a − 0.5 × 2 gives a = 8.5, and at x = 6, y = 8.5 − 3 = 5.5. The value 8.5 is the intercept.

questions.stem: A line of good fit for plant growth is y = 3 + 1.2x, where x is hours of sunlight per day and y is growth (cm). A plant with 10 hours of sunlight grew 18 cm. Compared with the prediction, it grew:
options: 6 cm less
3 cm more
3 cm less
1.2 cm more
questions.explanation: The prediction is 3 + 1.2 × 10 = 15 cm, and the plant grew 18 cm, which is 3 cm more than predicted. Its point lies above the line.

questions.stem: A line of good fit drawn by eye has 7 of the 10 data points above it and 3 below, spread along its length. The best adjustment is to:
options: make the line steeper, so it passes through the origin
rotate it until it passes through more of the points
move the line up, so points are balanced above and below
move the line down, so it passes below more points
questions.explanation: Most points lie above the line, so it sits too low. Raising it brings the points into balance on either side, which is what a line of good fit by eye should achieve.

questions.stem: Weekly sales are modelled by y = 220 + 15x, where x is advertising spend in hundreds of dollars. Increasing spending from $400 to $1000 predicts an increase in weekly sales of:
questions.explanation: In the model’s units x rises from 4 to 10, an increase of 6, so sales rise by 15 × 6 = 90. Using dollars, 600 × 15, ignores that x is measured in hundreds.

questions.stem: A line of good fit y = 5 + 0.4x was fitted to data with x-values from 20 to 60. Which prediction is the most reliable?
options: y = 23 at x = 45
y = 37 at x = 80
y = 5 at x = 0
y = 41 at x = 45
questions.explanation: The value x = 45 lies inside the data, so it is an interpolation, and 5 + 0.4 × 45 = 23. Predictions at 80 and 0 are extrapolations, and 41 uses double the slope.
